problem_summary.summary: Rotate a singly linked list to the right by k positions.
problem_summary.input_output: Inputs: possibly-null ListNode head and non-negative k. Return the rotated ListNode head. The judge supplies ListNode { int val; ListNode next; }.

brute_force.explanation: Count nodes, reduce k modulo the length, then perform that many one-position right rotations by moving the tail to the front each time.
brute_force.correctness_idea: A single operation moves the last node to the head, exactly one right rotation. Repeating the normalized number of rotations yields the requested shift.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n + n*r), where r = k mod n; worst case O(n^2).

optimized.explanation: Find the length and tail, connect tail to head to form a ring, then break the ring after node length - (k mod length) steps from the old head.
optimized.correctness_idea: A right rotation by r makes the node at index n-r the new head. The temporary ring lets the suffix become the prefix; breaking just before that node yields the required list.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — one length scan and at most one more linear walk.

steps.event: Measure the list and reduce the rotation.
steps.condition: The list has five nodes and k is smaller than length.
steps.action: Compute new tail position length - rotations = 3.

steps.event: Temporarily link the old tail to the old head.
steps.action: Make the chain circular and advance to the new tail at index 2.

steps.event: Break the ring after the new tail.
steps.condition: The next node after the new tail starts the rotated prefix.
steps.action: Set newTail.next to null and return newHead.

edge_cases.case: k is zero or a multiple of the length
edge_cases.handling: The optimized method returns before forming a ring; the baseline performs zero rotations.
Both methods normalize it with modulo before rotating.
